description:
Hermes agent just shipped computer use — and most setup guides will quietly route your screenshots through someone else's cloud. This one doesn't.

Start using Venice TODAY: https://venice.ai 

In this tutorial, I walk you through a fresh Hermes install pointed at Venice API (zero data retention) running Qwen 3.6 27B — an open-source private model that costs ~10x less than GPT 5.5 for similar capabilities. Then Hermes edits its own config, drops 97% of its token bloat, and starts driving a Mac as a personal digital janitor.

What you'll learn:
• How to install Hermes agent and add Venice as a custom endpoint provider
• Picking a private model from Venice (Qwen 3.6 27B, Kimi K2.6, Gemma 4 Uncensored) and the function-calling/reasoning/vision/code trade-offs
• Why skipping Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp matters for an agentic AI's privacy model
• Letting Hermes self-edit—pruning its own skills and tools from 5.2 MB to 160 KB before you do any work
• Activating computer use, installing the Cua driver, and granting the macOS Screen Recording + Accessibility permissions
• Practicing computer use on the Reminders app—organizing screenshots, archiving old downloads, building project-based todo lists
• Vibe-coding native macOS widgets directly through Hermes + Xcode

🔗 Resources 
Hermes Agent: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/ 
Venice API Custom Endpoint: https://docs.venice.ai/api-reference/api-spec  
Venice Models: https://docs.venice.ai/models/overview
